title: Torque pilot weekly throughput sync
summary: Weekly check-in for the Torque pilot. Reviewed last week's throughput numbers, observed a statistical tail in p50->p95 latency during 200-350 RPS bursts, discussed tradeoffs between raising concurrency targets vs longer batch windows. Confirmed KV cache warming artifacts and a queueing bump tied to a short-lived spike in request size. Agreed next steps: run an isolated burst experiment with KV cache prewarm, share updated perf spreadsheet and backlog of logs, adjust SE-controlled concurrency cap to 32 for the next 72-hour run, and validate rollback plan for fallback to smaller model variant. Also customer requested security artifacts for SSO/SAML and SOC2 checklist for private deploy evaluation.
action_items: Samir Patel - share updated pilot perf spreadsheet + raw tail logs via shared drive - due 2026-05-01
Jesse Ortega - schedule and run isolated 1-hour burst test with KV cache prewarm (concurrency cap=32) and capture p50/p95/p99 - due 2026-05-03
Marta Ruiz - provide sample request size distribution and a link to staging traffic generator - due 2026-05-02
Samir Patel - send SOC2/SSO integration summary and data residency note - due 2026-05-04
next_steps: Run 72-hour validation with new concurrency cap 32 and KV cache prewarm (Jesse to coordinate)
Helionix to run traffic generator with sampled payload mix and share results folder
Redwood to provide quick rollback script and instructions for switching to model-lean variant on surge
AE to follow up with pricing worksheet reflecting burst capacity add-on for dedicated pool
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-29 15:00 PDT | Duration 48m | Attendees: Samir (Redwood), Jesse (Redwood SE), Marta (Helionix), Devon, Arun

00:00 Samir: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, quick roll call?
00:04 Marta: Marta here, hi.
00:06 Devon: Devon here.
00:08 Arun: Arun here.
00:10 Samir: awesome, so quick agenda — one, brief perf recap; two, triage the p95 tail we saw during yesterday's ramp; three, decide next runs and owners. Anything else?
00:22 Marta: no that's good. Also we wanna confirm security docs for private eval.
00:27 Samir: yep we'll cover that at the end.
00:30 Jesse: jumping in on perf, I pulled the dashboard and also the raw logs, key observation: during the 220-350 RPS zone we saw a bimodal latency — bulk at ~120ms p50 but p95 spikes to ~950ms for some requests. The histogram correlated with a subset of large payloads and also cold KV cache hits.
00:52 Devon: when you say KV cache, you mean the prefix/key-value cache on the model runtime? We call it K V cash in our notes sometimes.
00:58 Jesse: yes that cache — apologies for phonetics. The runtime had a warm percentage drop from 98% to ~76% for a short window after a burst. That maps to requests routed to a node that hadn't primed its KV.
01:12 Marta: interesting — we do have a micro-batch of large attachments during that period, that could explain it. We use mixed token lengths, sometimes 4k tokens.
01:22 Samir: ok that helps. Two knobs discussed earlier: raise concurrency targets so more in-flight requests allow batching to absorb variance, or increase max_batch_wait (longer batching window) to get bigger batches at cost of latency. Thoughts?
01:36 Arun: if we raise concurrency, risk is we run into memory pressure on the GPU, right? Our infra team needs predictability.
01:42 Jesse: correct. On our side we recommend incremental increases. We suggested moving from cap 20 to 32 as a middle ground; that increases batching opportunities without huge mem footprint jump for this model.
01:53 Devon: what's the expected p50/p95 improvement if we do 32?
01:56 Jesse: from the sim it reduces p95 by roughly 20-30% in the 200-350 RPS band, p50 stays similar. But that assumes KV cache is warm. If cache misses continue you'll still see outliers.
02:10 Marta: do we have a simple way to prewarm the KV cache on the nodes before a scheduled ramp?
02:14 Jesse: yes we can run a targeted prewarm step — replay a sample of common prefixes to the host set. It'll take maybe 3-5 minutes to hit warm state for the active routing set.
02:24 Samir: good. So action: Jesse will run an isolated one-hour burst test with prewarm and concurrency=32 and capture p50/p95/p99.
02:33 Jesse: noted. I'll also capture per-node cache hit ratios and queue depths.
02:37 Devon: queue depth — we saw a small backlog in the routing queue, was that due to short GC pause?
02:43 Jesse: there's a small chance the node's GC / thread pause plus the larger payload serialization caused the backlog; logs show a few ~80ms serialization pauses on the staging side.
02:55 Arun: on rollback/fallback: if we see sustained tail we need an automatic fallback to a smaller model variant or to a hosted lower-latency tier. Is that supported?
03:05 Samir: yes, we have model variant fallback policies in the routing layer. We can define thresholds at the policy level — e.g., if p95 > 600ms for 5 minutes, route 30% to the lean model and notify. We can provide the playbook.
03:18 Marta: that'll be important for our SREs. Also on security: can you send the SOC2 checklist and notes on SSO/SAML integration? Our compliance team wants that before we move to private eval.
03:28 Samir: will do. I'll attach the SOC2 summary and the SAML SSO step-by-step.
03:33 Devon: pricing question — if we enable burst capacity for dedicated pool during business hours only, what's the cost model?
03:40 Samir: two options — hourly burst add-on that bills on peak reservation minutes, or a commit-based tier with discount for predictable burst windows. I'll send a pricing worksheet tailored to Helionix's expected burst profile.
03:52 Marta: great. On instrumentation — can you add tagging to the traces so we can separate our staging traffic generator from real production? Right now trace labels are generic.
03:59 Jesse: yes we can add a traffic tag header and we'll plumb that into the console. We'll also add token-level breakdowns per route so you can slice by payload size buckets.
04:12 Arun: any support for on-prem/hybrid? Our security folks prefer VPC or air-gapped options.
04:18 Samir: yes Redwood Private is available; we'll send the deck with deployment options, KMS/HSM integration notes, and the audit log retention SLAs.
04:27 Marta: ping — we also need a lightweight rollback script in case the concurrency bump causes perf regressions.
04:32 Jesse: I can prepare a short script that sets concurrency cap back to 20 and triggers cache eviction and a quick warm pass.
04:39 Samir: perfect. Let's capture owners — Jesse will run the burst prewarm test; Samir will share the spreadsheets and security docs; Marta will provide sampled payload distribution and the staging traffic generator link.
04:49 Marta: I'll share that in the shared folder.
04:52 Devon: quick nit — we experienced one request with an odd tokenization causing huge seq len; might be a client-side bug. We'll scrub client logs and share sample.
04:59 Samir: thanks. Any blockers on the plan?
05:02 Marta: no blockers. Timeline fine.
05:04 Samir: recap and next steps — Jesse runs isolated 1-hour prep test (due 2026-05-03), then we run 72-hour validation with concurrency=32 and prewarm; Samir sends SOC2/SSO docs and pricing worksheet; Marta shares traffic generator and distributions. We'll reconvene after initial 1-hour test results.
05:22 Devon: sounds good.
05:24 Arun: thanks everyone.
05:25 Samir: thanks all, end call.

Post-call notes: Jesse to attach per-node KV hit ratios and queue depth time series; Samir to flag possible burst add-on pricing, include a short rollback script in the repo. Links referenced: perf spreadsheet (drive.redwood/example-perf), SOC2 summary (docs.redwood/soc2-summary), staging traffic generator (helionix/staging-gen link).
